rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: At al-Hudaybiyya, lice badly afflicted Kaʿb; the Prophet ordered him to shave and prescribed the verse’s expiation options.
rows.anchor: عن كعب بن عجرة، قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says this report establishes that expiation is due after shaving, rejecting the claim that one must expiate first and shave afterward.
rows.anchor: وهذا الخبر ينبئ عن أن الصحيح من القول أن الفدية إنما تجب على الحالق بعد الحلق، وفساد قول من قال: يفتدي، ثم يحلق

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: Kaʿb reports that the Prophet prescribed three fasting days or food distributed among six poor people.
rows.anchor: عن كعب بن عجرة أنه قال

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: Kaʿb says the verse was revealed in response to his head ailment, first specifically for him and then as a general rule.
rows.anchor: قعدت إلى كعب وهو في المسجد، فسألته عن هذه الآية

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: Kaʿb recounts that lice covered his head and facial hair while on pilgrimage; after shaving, he was told to fast three days or feed six, and says the ruling became general.
rows.anchor: سمعت كعب بن عجرة يقول

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: At al-Hudaybiyya, lice fell from Kaʿb’s face as he cooked; the Prophet ordered him to shave and gave fasting, feeding, or sacrifice as alternatives.
rows.anchor: عن كعب بن عجرة، قال:

rows.speaker: أيوب
rows.claim: Ayyub notes uncertainty about which of the listed expiation choices the Prophet named first.
rows.anchor: قال أيوب: لا أدري بأيتهن بدأ

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: Kaʿb’s account has the Prophet ask whether the lice harmed him, then prescribe whichever expiation was feasible.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، عن كعب

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: A report through Qatāda says the Hudaybiyya incident led to shaving and a choice of sacrifice, three days of fasting, or feeding six people.
rows.anchor: عن صالح بن أبي الخليل، عن مجاهد، عن كعب بن عجرة

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى
rows.claim: A report from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā recalls the Prophet passing Kaʿb at al-Hudaybiyya with lice falling from his head and commanding him to shave.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، عن كعب بن عجرة

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: At al-Hudaybiyya, the Prophet asked about Kaʿb’s lice and offered sacrifice, three days of fasting, or feeding six; the food measure is three ṣāʿ.
rows.anchor: عن كعب بن عجرة، قال: مر بي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الحديبية، وأنا أوقد تحت قدر

rows.speaker: أيوب
rows.claim: Ayyūb’s version says to perform a sacrifice; Ibn Abī Najīḥ’s version specifies slaughtering a sheep.
rows.anchor: قال أيوب: انسك نسيكة. وقال ابن أبي نجيح: اذبح شاة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: In another account, the companions at al-Hudaybiyya still hoped to enter Mecca when the Prophet ordered Kaʿb to shave and offered the three expiation choices.
rows.anchor: حدثني عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، عن كعب بن عجرة

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: Kaʿb says the revelation came while the Muslims were under siege at al-Hudaybiyya in ihrām and lice were falling onto his face.
rows.anchor: عن كعب بن عجرة، قال:

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: Kaʿb insists the verse was revealed about him personally; in this report, the sacrifice means a sheep.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن كعب بن عجرة، قال:

rows.speaker: أبو مالك
rows.claim: Abū Mālik explains the options as three fasting days, feeding six people, or sacrificing a sheep.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، عن أبي مالك

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ gives the same specification: three fasting days, food for six, or a sheep.
rows.anchor: عبد الملك بن أبي سليمان، عن عطاء، مثله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid likewise identifies the alternatives as three days’ fasting, feeding six, or a sheep.
rows.anchor: عن عثمان بن الأسود، عن مجاهد، مثله

rows.speaker: إبراهيم ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm and Mujāhid say the sacrifice is a sheep or more, alongside three fasting days or feeding six.
rows.anchor: عن مغيرة، عن إبراهيم، ومجاهد، أنهما قالا في قوله

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: Kaʿb specifies three fasting days, a sheep or more, or three ṣāʿ of dates divided among six people.
rows.anchor: عن الشعبي، عن عبد الله بن معقل، عن كعب بن عجرة، أنه قال

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says each prohibited act entails one expiation; the person chooses among fasting three days, feeding six half a ṣāʿ each, or a sheep or more, and the verse concerns Kaʿb.
rows.anchor: عن السدي: {فمن كان منكم مريضا أو به أذى من رأسه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid extends the expiation to illness or harm from cupping, oil, medical treatment, or shaving lice, with the same three options.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says shaving before the offering reaches its place incurs expiation; he specifies three fasts, feeding six with one ṣāʿ per pair, or a sheep.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع : {ولا تحلقوا رءوسكم حتى يبلغ الهدي محله}

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the person expiates by fasting one day for each two mudd of food, one mudd for food and one for its accompaniment.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال:

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī specifies three fasting days, three ṣāʿ distributed among six people, or a sheep.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن مرة، عن عبد الله بن سلمة، قال: سئل علي، رضي الله عنه عن قول الله

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb reports that the Prophet prescribed three fasting days, six poor people, or a sheep.
rows.anchor: عن حرب بن قيس، مولى يحيى بن أبي طلحة، أنه سمع محمد بن كعب وهو يذكر الرجل الذي نزل فيه

rows.speaker: علقمة
rows.claim: ʿAlqama says a pilgrim blocked after entering ihrām sends a sheep; premature shaving, perfume, or medical treatment incurs three fasts, three ṣāʿ among six, or a sheep.
rows.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن إبراهيم، عن علقمة

rows.speaker: إبراهيم ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm and Mujāhid give the expiation as three days of fasting, three ṣāʿ divided among six, or a sheep.
rows.anchor: عن منصور، عن إبراهيم، ومجاهد، قوله: {ففدية من صيام أو صدقة أو نسك}

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another group argues that shaving for harm, applying perfume due to illness, or another prohibited act while in ihrām requires ten fasting days or feeding ten people.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: الواجب عليه إذا حلق رأسه من أذى، أو تطيب لعلة من مرض

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan allows choosing among the expiations but sets fasting at ten days or feeding ten people two makūk each, one of dates and one of wheat; the sacrifice is a sheep.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {ففدية من صيام أو صدقة أو نسك}

rows.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and ʿIkrima are cited for feeding ten people as the food expiation.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن، وعكرمة: {ففدية من صيام أو صدقة أو نسك}

rows.speaker: قائلو هذا القول
rows.claim: Supporters of the ten-person view analogize expiation for prohibited acts in ihrām to tamattuʿ: ten fasting days replace an unavailable offering, so feeding must correspond to ten days.
rows.anchor: وقاس قائلو هذا القول كل صيام وجب على محرم، أو صدقة؛ جزاء من نقص دخل في إحرامه

rows.speaker: قائلو هذا القول
rows.claim: They also argue that Qurʾānic substitution of food for fasting in Ramadan supports feeding one person for each required fasting day.
rows.anchor: فإن الله جل وعز أقام إطعام مسكين مكان صوم يوم لمن عجز عن الصوم في رمضان

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view requires a sheep if available; otherwise its value is converted to money and then food, or one fast for each half ṣāʿ if no food is available.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل الواجب على الحالق النسك شاة إن كانت عنده

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr answers that food is required first; if affordable, buy a sheep, otherwise convert its value to food, and if that is unavailable, fast a day per half ṣāʿ.
rows.anchor: سأل إبراهيم سعيد بن جبير، عن هذه الآية

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says hunting compensation is valued as food if the game is unavailable, and if food is unavailable one fasts a day per mudd; the same applies to this expiation.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قال

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another group holds that the person may freely choose any of the three expiation forms.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل هو مخير بين الخلال الثلاث يفتدي بأيها شاء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets Qurʾānic alternatives joined by “or” as a choice among options, not a required sequence.
rows.anchor: عن سيف بن سليمان، عن مجاهد، قال

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: In another formulation, Mujāhid says where the text says “or this or that,” the person may choose either; where it says “whoever does not find,” the first option comes first.
rows.anchor: عن ليث، عن مجاهد، قال

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the expiation verse lets the person choose whichever option he wants.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، وسئل عن قوله

rows.speaker: عطاء وعمرو بن دينار
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and ʿAmr ibn Dīnār say the person may choose any of the expiation options.
rows.anchor: قال لي عطاء، وعمرو بن دينار، في قوله

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ generalizes that every Qurʾānic “or” clause gives a choice.
rows.anchor: ابن جريج، قال: قال عطاء

rows.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār likewise says that a Qurʾānic “or” clause allows the person to take whichever option he wishes.
rows.anchor: قال لي عمرو بن دينار

rows.speaker: عطاء ومجاهد
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and Mujāhid say any Qurʾānic “or this or that” construction leaves the choice to the person.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء، ومجاهد، أنهما قالا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says alternatives joined by “or” are optional, while constructions beginning “whoever” follow their stated sequence.
rows.anchor: عن ليث، ومجاهد، عن ابن عباس، قال

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says the person may choose among expiations introduced by “or,” but “whoever does not find” requires the first option in order.
rows.anchor: ثنا داود، عن عكرمة، قال

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says every Qurʾānic “or” clause gives a choice.
rows.anchor: عن أيوب، قال: حدثت عن عطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers free choice among the three expiations because the Prophet offered Kaʿb a sheep, three fasting days, or food for six at half a ṣāʿ each, without restricting him to one.
rows.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندنا ما ثبت به الخبر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues that God left the choice open and that denying choice conflicts with the community’s agreement on choosing among the three expiations for a broken oath.
rows.anchor: لأن الله لم يحصره على واحدة منهن بعينها، فلا يجوز له أن يعدوها إلى غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He challenges opponents to explain why shaving expiation would precede shaving while tamattuʿ and oath expiations would not precede their acts; the same reasoning applies to both.
rows.anchor: وأما الزاعمون أن كفارة الحلق قبل الحلق، فإنه يقال لهم: أخبرونا عن الكفارة للمتمتع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says an oath expiation before the oath is invalid by consensus, and challenges any distinction from the timing of shaving expiation.
rows.anchor: أنها غير مجزئة قبل الحلف بإجماع

rows.speaker: علقمة
rows.claim: ʿAlqama interprets “when you are secure” as recovery from the illness that had prevented pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن إبراهيم، عن علقمة

rows.speaker: عروة
rows.claim: ʿUrwa says a person recovering from the injury or illness that caused obstruction must proceed to the House and remain in ihrām until arriving there.
rows.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، في قوله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets security as freedom from fear, noting that the people were afraid at the time.
rows.anchor: ثنا سعيد، عن قتادة، قوله

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ combines the senses: one is safe from fear and has recovered from illness.
rows.anchor: حدثت عن عمار بن الحسن، قال: ثنا ابن أبي جعفر، عن أبيه، عن الربيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers security from fear because security is the opposite of fear, not illness; only a difficult and less direct reading treats it as safety from feared death in illness.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول أشبه بتأويل الآية، لأن الأمن هو خلاف الخوف، لا خلاف المرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the passage to al-Ḥudaybiyya: the companions feared the enemy, and God explained what they owed if enemy fear blocked pilgrimage and when that fear ended.
rows.anchor: لأن هذه الآيات نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أيام الحديبية، وأصحابه من العدو خائفون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī paraphrases the verse: when the blocked believers become secure and perform ʿumra leading into hajj, they owe whatever offering is available.
rows.anchor: فعليكم ما استيسر من الهدي

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr defines the relevant tamattuʿ as a pilgrim blocked by enemy, illness, injury, or another obstacle until hajj days pass, then converting hajj to ʿumra and remaining released until next year’s hajj with an offering.
rows.anchor: سمعت ابن الزبير، وهو يخطب وهو يقول

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports Ibn al-Zubayr’s view that tamattuʿ applies only to the person who was blocked.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن عطاء، قال: كان ابن الزبير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this tamattuʿ applies both to the blocked pilgrim and to one whose route was left open.
rows.anchor: قال: وقال ابن عباس: «هي لمن أحصر

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the pilgrim first sends an offering when blocked and exits ihrām; after safety, he performs a delayed ʿumra in hajj months, then remains released until hajj and owes an offering.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: فإن أحصرتم في حجكم فما استيسر من الهدي

rows.speaker: علقمة
rows.claim: ʿAlqama says a blocked pilgrim sends a sheep; if he recovers, reaches the House, and completes the hajj with ʿumra, he must perform hajj the following year.
rows.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن إبراهيم، عن علقمة

rows.speaker: علقمة
rows.claim: If the blocked pilgrim returns without going on to the House, ʿAlqama says he owes hajj, ʿumra, and blood for delaying ʿumra; if he returns as a tamattuʿ pilgrim in hajj months, he owes a sheep or, if unable, ten fasts split three during hajj and seven after return.
rows.anchor: وإن هو رجع ولم يتم إلى البيت من وجهه ذلك، فإن عليه حجة، وعمرة، ودما لتأخيره العمرة
